title: 1992 AHSME Problem 12
statement: Let \(y=mx+b\) be the image when the line \(x-3y+11=0\) is reflected across the \(x\)-axis. The value of \(m+b\) is

solutions.text:
A point \((x,y)\) is on the reflected line exactly when \((x,-y)\) is on the original line. Hence \(x+3y+11=0,\) or \[ y=-\frac13x-\frac{11}{3}. \] Therefore \(m+b=-\frac13-\frac{11}{3}=-4.\)

Thus the correct answer is C.
hints: Reflection across the \(x\)-axis replaces each \(y\)-coordinate by its negative
Replace \(y\) by \(-y\) in the original equation, then solve for \(y\)
